title: Tariff Value and Minimum Value Determination
summary: This thread tracks the evolution of minimum import values and tariff values for various goods. Over time, the mechanism shifted from simple list updates to more structured, sector-specific valuation frameworks for customs duty assessment.

evolution.legal_basis: Transitioned from Customs Act 1969 to Customs Act 2023.
evolution.structure: Shifted from static lists to dynamic, sector-specific minimum value schedules.

timeline.change: Removal of Heading 17.01 entries from Table-2.
Insertion of new values for Heading 17.01 (Raw sugar).
Comprehensive update of tariff values for various goods.
Introduction of 'temporary' determination for minimum values.
Formalization of minimum value lists for customs duty assessment.
Updated minimum value schedule for tariff calculation.
Updated tariff values for raw sugar.
Consolidation of minimum value lists under the new Customs Act 2023.
Comprehensive replacement of Table-2 with updated minimum values for food and industrial goods.

এস.আর.ও. নং ১৪২-আইন/২০১৭/২৮/কাস্টমস ।- Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969), Gi section 25 Gi sub-section (3) ‡Z cÖ`Ë ক্ষমতাবলে সরকার, এই বিভাগের ১৯ জ্যৈষ্ঠ, ১৪২৩ বঙ্গাব্দ মোতাবেক ২ জুন, ২০১৬ খ্রিষ্টাব্দ তারিখের প্রজ্ঞাপন এস.আর.ও. নং ১৬৫-আইন/২০১৬/২৭/ কাস্টমস এর নিম্নরূপ অধিকতর সংশোধন করিল, যথা:-

উপরিউক্ত প্রজ্ঞাপনের-
(ক) প্রস্তাবনায় উল্লিখিত “নির্ধারণ করিল” শব্দগুলির পরিবর্তে “সাময়িকভাবে নির্ধারণ করিল” শব্দগুলি প্রতিস্থাপিত হইবে;

“ব্যাখ্যা।- (১) “ন্যূনতম মূল্য” অর্থ আমদানিকৃত সাধারণ মানসম্পন্ন পণ্যের লেনদেন মূল্য, তবে উন্নত মানসম্পন্ন পণ্যের মূল্য নির্ধারিত ন্যূনতম মূল্য অপেক্ষা অধিকতর হওয়া যুক্তিযুক্ত।
(২) “Renowned brand” অর্থ খ্যাতনামা বা বহুল প্রচলিত বা বিখ্যাত ব্র্যান্ড।
(৩) “General brand” অর্থ “Renowned brand” নয় এইরূপ কোন ব্র্যান্ড।”।

Customs Act 1969: Section 25(3) of this Act empowers the Government to issue notifications regarding tariff and minimum values of goods.
The current order utilizes the legal authority granted under the Act to amend a previously issued S.R.O.
S.R.O. 165-AIN/2016: This notification is formally amended to revise tariff and minimum value criteria for various categories of goods.
Specific terminology within the original notification is replaced with new definitions to provide clarification on valuation standards.
TABLE-1: This table provides the tariff values in US dollars per unit for specific imported commodities, including tea, sugar, and petroleum products.
The values listed serve as a basis for assessment as part of the formal amendment to the existing tariff order.
TABLE-2: This table outlines the minimum values in US dollars per unit for a wide range of goods such as food preparations, personal care items, plastics, and electronics.
The minimum value is established to reflect the standard transaction price for general quality goods, while allowing for higher valuation for premium products.
Imported Goods: The order defines and updates the valuation framework for various imported goods by categorizing them into tables based on their tariff or minimum value.
Valuation criteria distinguish between general brands and renowned brands, with specific conditions applied based on the country of origin or technical specifications.
Value: The order introduces an explanatory note defining minimum value as the transaction value for general quality imported goods, while acknowledging that superior quality goods should naturally command a higher price.
Brand classification between Renowned and General is explicitly defined to assist in the consistent application of these values.

Customs Act 1969: Section 25(3) of this Act empowers the Government to determine tariff values and minimum values for imported goods to facilitate the assessment and imposition of Customs Duty.
TABLE-1: This table lists specific goods identified by their Heading and H.S. Code, establishing their respective tariff values in US dollars per unit for the assessment of ad valorem Customs Duty.
TABLE-2: This table specifies the minimum values for a wide range of imported goods, categorized by their Heading and H.S. Code, to serve as the basis for calculating Customs Duty.
Renowned Brand: This term is defined as a famous, widely prevalent, or reputable brand for the purposes of this SRO.

(ক) “Renowned Brand” অর্থখ্যাতনামা বা বহুল প্রচলিত বা বিখ্যাত ব্র্যান্ড;

(খ) “General Brand” অর্থ Renowned Brand নহে এইরূপ কোনো ব্র্যান্ড।

Customs Act 2023: The Government issued this order under the authority granted by Section 27(5) of the Customs Act 2023.
Customs Duty: This order establishes tariff values and minimum values for specific imported goods to be used for the purpose of assessing and imposing customs duty.
TABLE-1: Table-1 specifies tariff values per unit for various crude oils and motor spirits listed by their respective HS codes.
TABLE-2: Table-2 defines minimum values per unit for a wide range of goods, including food items, household appliances, electronics, textiles, and construction materials, to serve as a baseline for customs valuation.
Renowned Brand: The term is defined for the purposes of this order to mean a famous, well-known, or widely recognized brand.
General Brand: The term is defined for the purposes of this order to mean any brand that does not qualify as a Renowned Brand.

TABLE-2: This instrument replaces the existing TABLE-2 with a newly specified table containing minimum tariff values for various imported goods.
The updated table includes specific HS codes, descriptions, units of measurement, and minimum US dollar values for customs valuation purposes across multiple commodity sectors.
Value: For furnace oil, the customs valuation must be determined using internationally recognized price sources such as Platts if international market prices fluctuate.
For smart phones and cellular telephones, if manufacturer-published pricing is available on official websites, those prices must be used to determine the dutiable value.
Imported Goods or Raw Materials: A wide range of commodities, including meat, dairy, produce, spices, textiles, electronics, and vehicle parts, are assigned specific minimum per-unit values for customs assessment.
Specialized valuation conditions are applied to goods like ceramic tiles based on size, petroleum products based on market sources, and mobile phones based on manufacturer data.
Import Policy Order: The valuation of used motor vehicle parts is subject to the specific conditions outlined for controlled goods within the existing import policy framework.
